messages:
elaine.sales: Hey team — Acme sent back the SIG/CAIQ and circled the encryption / KMS section. They want a short, presales-friendly blurb that covers: at-rest encryption, BYOK options, HSM support for on-prem, key rotation responsibilities, and any limitations for Hosted vs Private. Also asking how long a POC for on-prem HSM integration would take. Can someone draft answers I can drop in the CAIQ?

sam.security: Short top-level answer you can paste: we encrypt customer data at rest and in transit. For Hosted (Redwood API) we use envelope encryption with service-managed keys by default; customers can opt for customer-managed keys (BYOK) via cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for additional key ownership controls. For Private deployments we support attaching an HSM or PKCS#11-compatible key manager (customer-provided) so the root key material never leaves the customer's boundary. We also support HSM-backed key import for cloud KMS where supported.

sam.security: A few useful one-liners for CAIQ: 
- At-rest: All persisted model artifacts and user data are encrypted with AES-256; service uses envelope encryption + per-tenant DEKs.
- BYOK: Supported for AWS/GCP/Azure KMS via CMKs; import / external-HSM options available for Private deployments.
- HSM: For Private installs we integrate with PKCS#11 HSMs or cloud HSM offerings; keys can be configured to be non-exportable.
- Rotation: Service keys rotated periodically; customer-managed keys are rotated per customer policy (we provide tooling to rewrap and migrate).

aria.eng: Adding ops-level detail for the POC and caveats: 
- POC prerequisites: network routes (outbound to our control plane for Private-managed installs OR direct peering for fully air-gapped), PKCS#11 endpoint or cloud KMS ARN, service account with import/reimport rights if using cloud KMS, and a test key with the correct capabilities (encrypt/decrypt, sign if needed).
- Timeline: baseline Private-deployment HSM POC = 2–3 weeks assuming certificates, IP allowlist, and HSM access are available day 0. If customer needs on-site HSM install + secure courier, add 1–2 weeks.
- Known limitations: Hosted API customers cannot plug a customer HSM into our shared multi-tenant hosted fleet; that requires Dedicated or Private. For Hosted BYOK the flow is typically CMK referencing + grant-based access.

aria.eng: Example snippet for our Private config (feel free to paste into pre-sales doc):
```
key_management:
  provider: pkcs11
  endpoint: "https://hsm.example.internal:8443"
  token_label: "acme-prod-token"
  key_label: "acme-root-key"
  non_exportable: true
```

mike.sales: This is great. Can we also add a short paragraph on rotation responsibilities? Customer wants to know who rotates what.

sam.security: Sure: 
- Service-managed keys: Redwood rotates service key material on a regular schedule (we rotate intermediate/service keys every 90 days) and maintain key versioning + CI to rewrap DEKs. Rotation is transparent to customers.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK/CMK): Rotation of the customer root/CMK is controlled by the customer. Redwood will rewrap DEKs to the new CMK version on request or via an agreed automation run; for imported keys (where key material never leaves HSM) Redwood cannot perform root rotation; customer must provide a new key version/import, then we perform a rewrap migration.
- HSM (Private): If keys are non-exportable in customer HSM, rotation is performed inside the HSM by the customer or their ops team; Redwood supports on-request re-encryption/rewrap once new key version is available.

sam.security: Add a short note about audit evidence: we can provide KMS event logs, CMK usage logs, and for Private installs we can produce HSM audit logs (assuming customer provides access/collection). Also we can provide a short architecture diagram for CAIQ.

elaine.sales: Perfect. Quick QA for the CAIQ entry: customer asked whether we hold plaintext during any step — need a concise sentence.

aria.eng: Concise: Redwood never persists unencrypted customer plaintext at rest. During active inference a transient in-memory plaintext buffer exists on serving hosts; we minimize retention, control via memory protections and immediate garbage collection, and do not persist those buffers to disk. That sentence should be fine for SIG.

mike.sales: I'll schedule a 30-min sync with Acme next week. @elaine.sales can you paste the CAIQ answers into a doc and drop the link here? I can forward to them with notes about timeline.

sec-review-bot: :white_check_mark: SIG encryption checklist updated — fields for At-Rest Encryption, BYOK, HSM, Key Rotation populated by sam.security and aria.eng.

elaine.sales: Pasting the short bundle for CAIQ (wording optimized for presales):
- At-rest encryption: All persisted customer data and model artifacts are encrypted with AES-256 using envelope encryption (unique DEKs per tenant).
- In-transit encryption: TLS 1.2+ for all control and data-plane traffic; mutual TLS available for Private deployments.
- BYOK / CMK: Supported. For Hosted customers, BYOK is available via supported cloud KMS (AWS/GCP/Azure). For Dedicated/Private, customers may attach their HSM or PKCS#11-compatible key manager so key material remains under customer control.
- HSM support: Private deployments integrate with customer-provided HSMs (PKCS#11) or cloud HSMs. Keys can be configured as non-exportable.
- Key rotation: Redwood rotates service-managed keys regularly (intermediate/service keys ~90d). Customer-managed keys are rotated by the customer; Redwood will assist with rewrapping/migration on request. For imported non-exportable keys, rotation must be performed in the HSM and then a new key/version is provided for rewrap.
- Proofs & logs: We can provide KMS access logs, CloudAudit trails, and HSM audit records for Private deployments as part of the vendor review process.

elaine.sales: @mike.sales dropping this into the CAIQ now. If Acme asks for a POC statement of work, aria — can you paste a 1-paragraph SOW blurb we can use?

aria.eng: SOW blurb: "Eng will run a Private HSM integration POC: validate PKCS#11 connectivity, import or reference a test key, perform end-to-end request encryption/decryption, and validate rewrap/migration workflow. Deliverables: test runbook, connectivity checklist, recorded logs demonstrating key operations, and a short remediation list. Estimated effort: 2–3 weeks from kickoff given access and allowlists."

mike.sales: Nice. I'm good to go — thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

elaine.sales: Thanks all — I'll share the CAIQ + SOW with Acme and open a follow-up thread if they want more granularity.

sec-review-bot: :lock: Reminder: for any customer requesting HSM-attached Private deployments, ensure legal has signed the addendum for on-prem key custody before kickoff.
